claims.claim: As of 2026-10-06, the U.S. de minimis administrative exemption for most low-value imports remains suspended; CBP's postal rule is in force.
claims.counterevidence: The policy is not an import ban; a new postal informal-entry process remains available, and some separate statutory exemptions survive.

claims.claim: CBP reports 74.8 million postal de-minimis entries in FY2024 versus 7,254,980 entries from September-November 2025, annualized to 29,099,645, about 61% below FY2024.
claims.counterevidence: CBP attributes the change to a combination of new duties, de minimis suspension and the interim mail process; the data do not isolate a single causal factor.

claims.claim: The removal of the old de minimis regime materially weakens the economics of very low-value direct-to-consumer arbitrage and raises data/compliance requirements.
claims.counterevidence: High-margin lightweight goods may still retain sufficient spreads, and the new process still permits low-value imports.

claims.claim: China-related Section 301 duties cannot be modeled as one universal rate; liability depends on HTS classification and exclusions, with 178 exclusions extended into November 2026.
claims.counterevidence: Many HTS classifications remain subject to additional duties, so individual frozen SKUs may still face substantial tariff burden.

claims.claim: AliExpress has large-scale mechanisms capable of compressing China-to-overseas spreads: it covers more than 200 countries and regions, introduced AliExpressDirect using inventories in more than 30 countries, and reported operating profit in the June 2026 quarter driven partly by logistics optimization and cost efficiency.
claims.counterevidence: Scale, profitability and local inventory do not establish exact-SKU coverage of China-domestic head products or prove price parity.

claims.claim: PDD identifies de minimis removal as a risk that can increase consumer prices and reduce orders or merchant participation, but PDD's consolidated Q2 2026 revenue still grew 8% year over year.
claims.counterevidence: The Q2 financial results are consolidated and do not isolate Temu's U.S. economics.

claims.claim: Superbuy currently states that standard purchasing from Taobao, Tmall, JD and 1688 carries no purchasing service fee and that multiple items can be consolidated without a consolidation charge.
claims.counterevidence: International freight, customs, fuel/operation charges, payment costs and optional services remain separate costs.

claims.claim: Agent forwarding has structural logistics penalties: chargeable freight can use volumetric weight and batteries, appliances, liquids and other sensitive categories face route restrictions.
claims.counterevidence: Consolidation, package removal, vacuum packing and alternative routes can materially reduce some of these penalties.

claims.claim: Superbuy's published terms allocate substantial international logistics and customs risks to the user, and its no-reason return/exchange mechanism is principally a pre-international-shipment China-stage service.
claims.counterevidence: Insurance, claims assistance and re-delivery mechanisms can mitigate some losses.

claims.claim: Taobao's hosted legal statement prohibits unauthorized acquisition or use of platform content through robots, spiders or similar automated mechanisms.
claims.counterevidence: Authorized APIs, commercial partnerships, or user-side interaction could create a compliant data-access path; these were not verified in this workstream.

claims.claim: Cross-platform China sourcing and matching functionality has historical precedent: AiPrice's Chrome listing reports 100,000 users and supports image/product research across Amazon, AliExpress, 1688, Taobao and other platforms.
claims.counterevidence: AiPrice is primarily positioned toward sellers, sourcing and operations rather than a complete U.S.-consumer landed-cost routing product.

claims.claim: AiPrice's own forum contains 2026 reports of cross-platform search functions failing, providing anecdotal evidence that third-party matching integrations can be operationally brittle.
claims.counterevidence: Individual support incidents do not establish systemic or persistent failure.

claims.claim: Community evidence in 2026 shows both high forwarding costs and successful U.S. deliveries, implying substantial cost/time dispersion rather than categorical infeasibility.
claims.counterevidence: Community posts are self-selected anecdotes and cannot establish population-level shipping economics.

categories.counterevidence: Low-value imports remain possible under new entry processes.
No pre-freeze exact-SKU coverage or price comparison was performed.
Free procurement and consolidation preserve viability for some lightweight, high-spread goods.
Insurance and claims support can mitigate but not eliminate the consumer-experience gap.
Existing tool adoption proves technical demand/predecessors, but not the economics of a consumer landed-cost router.
